skill.name: install-anti-slop
skill.description: Install and configure the bundled anti-slop Oxlint plugin in a local TypeScript or JavaScript repository. Integrate its opinionated rules with existing lint configuration.
skill.summary: Add the bundled anti-slop plugin, dependencies, Oxlint configuration, and verification steps to an existing repository.
skill.author: dmmulroy

security_audit.summary: All 49 static findings are false positives caused by TypeScript imports, template literals, AST property names, or Markdown formatting. Semantic review found two medium risks: unchecked installer destinations and installation of unpinned current dependency versions.

remediation.issue: The installer accepts absolute paths and parent traversal, including with --force.
remediation.suggestion: Reject absolute destinations and verify the resolved target remains inside the current repository before creating directories or copying files.

remediation.issue: The procedure installs whichever dependency versions are current at execution time.
remediation.suggestion: Publish reviewed compatible versions, pin exact dependencies, and require explicit approval before updating those pins.

semantic_findings.title: Installer Allows Destinations Outside the Repository
semantic_findings.description: The installer resolves an unchecked destination argument against the current directory. Absolute paths or parent traversal can target files outside the repository, and --force permits overwrites.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The argument reaches path.resolve without a containment check before mkdirSync and cpSync. The code directly confirms the out-of-repository write behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Installation Uses Unpinned Current Dependency Versions
semantic_findings.description: The procedure tells agents to discover and install current package versions. Results can change between runs and expose users immediately to a compromised upstream release.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly query current versions and install them. The named packages are legitimate, but the workflow lacks a reviewed version pin or integrity check.

content.value_statement: Adding opinionated Oxlint rules manually requires copying plugin files and merging configuration safely. This skill performs the integration while preserving existing project settings.
actual_capabilities: Inspects the repository package manager, lint configuration, and existing anti-slop files.
Copies the bundled Oxlint plugin into a project tooling directory.
Adds Oxlint and plugin dependencies using the repository package manager.
Merges plugin registration, ignore patterns, and fifteen rule settings into existing configuration.
Runs project lint and type checks, then reports remaining findings.
limitations: Requires an existing TypeScript or JavaScript repository with a supported Oxlint configuration.
May produce many lint findings because every bundled rule is enabled as an error.
Does not automatically repair application findings unless the user requests cleanup.
Dependency versions are discovered during installation and are not pinned by the skill.

prompt_templates.prompt: Install the anti-slop Oxlint plugin in this repository. Preserve existing configuration and report every changed file.
prompt_templates.scenario: A repository already uses Oxlint and needs the bundled rules.

prompt_templates.prompt: Add anti-slop using this repository's package manager. Run lint and type checks, then summarize unresolved findings.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants installation plus immediate validation.

prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate anti-slop with this Vite+ repository. Merge lint and format ignores, register the plugin, and run the full check.
prompt_templates.scenario: A Vite+ project needs configuration tailored to its check workflow.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing local anti-slop plugin before migration. Compare rules and diagnostics, preserve custom behavior, and explain every compatibility decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced repository has a modified or outdated local plugin.

best_practices: Review the working tree and existing lint configuration before installation.
Inspect dependency versions and the final diff before accepting changes.
Address new findings through clearer types and boundary parsing instead of weakening rule severity.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite an existing plugin copy before comparing its rules and diagnostics.
Do not replace existing ignore patterns or unrelated dependency ranges.
Do not suppress findings with unsafe casts or mechanical type changes.

faq.question: Which projects can use this skill?
faq.answer: It targets local TypeScript or JavaScript repositories that use Oxlint or Vite+ lint configuration.

faq.question: Which rules are installed?
faq.answer: The bundled plugin provides fifteen opinionated rules covering assertions, unknown types, reflection, dictionary types, mocking, and related patterns.

faq.question: Will it overwrite an existing plugin?
faq.answer: The installer refuses an existing destination by default. Forced replacement should occur only after backup and review.

faq.question: Does it fix every new lint finding?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and changes application code only when the user explicitly requests migration or cleanup.

faq.question: How are dependency versions selected?
faq.answer: The procedure queries current Oxlint and plugin versions, then installs matching versions with the repository package manager.

faq.question: What checks run after installation?
faq.answer: It runs the repository lint command and type check. Vite+ projects use the full project check.
